title: Phase 2 Entry Relaxation: min_conditions count-based entry for 3 templates
description: Replace overly restrictive AND-entry logic with count-based min_conditions parameter in 3 strategy templates: trend_following (4-way AND → count >= min_conditions), mean_reversion (AND entry → count >= min_conditions), volatility_breakout (5-way AND → count >= min_conditions). Also add RSI threshold ranges to param_space JSONs created in TASK-001. Defaults preserve current behavior: trend min_conditions=4, mean_reversion min_conditions=2, volatility_breakout min_conditions=5.
action: In trend_following.py __init__ add `self._min_conditions = p.get("min_conditions", 4)`. In generate_signals line 239 change `entries = trend_up & rsi_ok_long & vol_ok & atr_ok` to count-based: `condition_count = trend_up.astype(int) + rsi_ok_long.astype(int) + vol_ok.astype(int) + atr_ok.astype(int); entries = condition_count >= self._min_conditions`. Same pattern for exits with rsi_ok_short. In mean_reversion.py add `self._min_conditions = p.get("min_conditions", 2)`. Change line 129-132 from `vol_ok & (A | B)` to count-based where long_count = vol_ok.astype(int) + (rsi < oversold).astype(int) + (close < bb_lower).astype(int), entries_long = long_count >= min_conditions; same for short. In volatility_breakout.py add `self._min_conditions = p.get("min_conditions", 5)`. Change line 363-364 5-way AND to count-based. Update param_space JSONs with rsi_overbought/oversold ranges.

success_metrics: min_conditions=2 produces more or equal entries than min_conditions=4 for trend_following
All 3 default min_conditions match current behavior (4/2/5)

reference.pattern: Follow existing __init__ param extraction pattern: p.get('key', default) with type annotation. Follow existing generate_signals() pattern: compute boolean Series, then combine with astype(int) sum for count-based logic.

rationale.chosen_approach: Count-based min_conditions is backward compatible (defaults match current AND logic) while allowing optimizer to relax entry criteria. This directly addresses the 'overly restrictive AND-entry' gap identified in the analysis.
decision_factors: 4-way AND in trend_following means all 4 conditions must align simultaneously, producing very few signals
5-way AND in volatility_breakout is even more restrictive — statistically near-impossible on 4h bars
Count-based logic lets optimizer find the optimal threshold via win_rate objective from TASK-001
rationale.tradeoffs: Lower min_conditions may increase false signals, but the profit_target_exit from TASK-003 will cap losses on bad entries

risks: mean_reversion entry logic has OR structure (long OR short) — count-based must preserve the direction separation
volatility_breakout _latest_signal uses Python bool not pandas, so astype(int) won't work — use int() builtin instead
